fields.place: Born at Pañcakhaṇḍa; Navadvīpa (the first school of Nyāya); Mithilā
fields.notes: Student of Vāsudeva Sārvabhauma; the great logician of Navadvīpa, who set up the first school of Nyāya there (in Hari Ghoṣ's cattle-shed); author of the Cintāmaṇi-dīdhiti and other Nyāya works. Advaita-prakāśa 54: Lord Caitanya threw His own Nyāya commentary into the Gaṅgā so that Raghunātha's could spread.

Paternal grandfather of Lord Caitanya, of Baḍagaṅgā in Śrīhaṭṭa; Parjanya Gopa in Vraja (GGD 35). Wife Kalāvatī; seven sons — Kaṁsāri, Paramānanda, Padmanābha, Sarveśvara, Jagannātha (the fifth), Janārdana, Trailokyanātha. The Lord visited him at Baḍagaṅgā (his Caṇḍī manuscript found copied: Prema-vilāsa 24).

fields.place: Rājurā near Kāndrā (west of Kāṭoyā); Mayanāḍāl (his Deity of Mahāprabhu)
fields.notes: Born as a boon to Kālīcaraṇa Mitra of Rājurā through Maṅgala Ṭhākura (disciple of Gadādhara Paṇḍita), from whom he took dīkṣā at sixteen; installed Mahāprabhu's Deity at Mayanāḍāl; a kīrtana singer whose tunes gave the Manoharaśāhī style its name. His son Hare Kṛṣṇa Siddhapuruṣa; a family of kīrtanīyās and mṛdaṅga players.
